abstract: A case of choriocarcinoma of the urinary bladder is presented. A 57-year-old man underwent a cystectomy for transitional cell carcinoma, grade II. Choriocarcinoma was found, in addition to the transitional cell carcinoma, in the removed urinary bladder. After the operation, metastases appeared in both lungs, evolving rapidly despite chemotherapy. The patient died five months after admission. Immunohistochemically, staining for human placental lactogen was strongly positive, and both alpha and beta subunits of human chorionic gonadotropin were weakly positive in the primary site of the removed urinary bladder and in the metastatic foci.
abstract_ja: 57歳の男性が、Grade IIの移行上皮癌に対して膀胱摘除術を受けた。切除された膀胱には、移行上皮癌に加えて絨毛癌が認められた。術後、両肺に転移が出現し、化学療法にもかかわらず急速に進行した。患者は入院後5か月で死亡した。免疫組織化学染色では、切除された膀胱の原発巣および転移巣において、ヒト胎盤性ラクトゲンが強陽性を示し、ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)のαおよびβサブユニットはいずれも弱陽性であった。
